user.title: Air-to-water heat pump audit
user.description: There is still an entry of the predecessor “WP-Audit”. Its settings can be taken over.

import_legacy.title: Take over from WP-Audit
import_legacy.description: Taken over from “{title}”: entity mapping, plant data, events and the stored daily values of the timeline. All audits are enabled. Delete the old entry afterwards under Devices & services.

setup.title: Heat pump audit: profiles and audits
setup.description: Profiles suggest matching entities (interface) and data sheet values (model). Choose “None” if nothing fits – everything can be changed afterwards. Below, the audits that should run; more can be added later via “Add audit”.

signals.title: Heat pump audit: operating signals
signals.description: Assign the on/off signals of the heat pump. Every field is optional; checks without data become 'not assessable'.

data.heartbeat: Heartbeat (e.g. uptime of the data logger)

measurements.title: Heat pump audit: measurements
measurements.description: Electricity always from the meter, never from controller estimates.

data.outdoor_temp: Outdoor temperature of the heat pump

controller.title: Heat pump audit: controller values
controller.description: Used for plausibility checks in audit 0. A heat counter of the controller that keeps counting without Home Assistant fills data gaps in the daily values.

data.controller_dhw_consumed: Controller: electricity hot water, previous day

circuit.title: Heat pump audit: heating circuit and room
circuit.description: Only needed with a buffer tank or low loss header between heat pump and radiators, and for audit 2. Leave empty what does not exist.

dhw.title: Heat pump audit: hot water
dhw.description: For the hot water audit. The tank temperature is required, the setpoint optional.

tariff.title: Heat pump audit: tariff
tariff.description: Only for the cost audit and only if available: a sensor with the current electricity price (dynamic tariff, €/kWh) and a signal while the grid operator blocks or throttles the heat pump. Fixed prices are master data.

controls.title: Heat pump audit: controls
controls.description: Values the heat pump interface can write. If a role is assigned, the action column proposes a value an admin can apply with one click; the audit never changes anything by itself. Leave empty what the interface cannot do.

data.short_cycle_lockout: Lockout after a too short heating run (C3)
data.short_cycle_min_run: Minimum run time for the lockout (C3)

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already being audited.

init.title: Master data
init.description: Facts about the system that cannot be measured. Empty fields are allowed: the affected check then shows “not assessable – master data missing”.

plant.name: System

data_description.hydraulic_separation: How heat pump and heating circuit are connected. Decides whether the buffer loss (T1) is checked.
data_description.flow_rate_min_lpm: Smallest permitted heat pump flow rate according to the manufacturer (T4).
data_description.circuit_flow_max_lpm: Largest flow of the heating circuit pump according to the data sheet (highest curve at zero head); an upper bound regardless of the setting. The estimate in T3 never shows more (1 m³/h = 16.7 l/min).
data_description.capacity_min_table: Smallest heating capacity in kW per flow temperature and outdoor temperature (C4). Format (YAML): one line per flow temperature, below it indented outdoor: kW, e.g. "35:" followed by "-7: 3.9", "2: 3.5", "7: 3.5". Values in between are interpolated linearly.
data_description.immersion_heater_kw: Electric immersion heater in the cylinder (C5).
data_description.booster_heater_kw: Electric booster heater in the heating circuit (C5).

plant.description: Manufacturer data from the data sheet or installation manual.

data_description.dhw_tank_volume_l: Nominal volume from the rating plate (W4, W6).
data_description.cold_water_c: Annual mean; 10 °C without a better value (W6).
data_description.dhw_disinfection_interval_days: If the tank stays below 50 °C, W2 is green as long as it is heated to 60 °C at least this often. Legionella setting on the controller.

data_description.heating_hours: Hours with outdoor temperature below the heating limit (15 °C) at the site. Used to project starts per year (C1).
data_description.room_temp_target: Desired temperature in the reference room (T6).
data_description.heating_degree_days: Long-term average of heating degree days (base 20/15 °C) at the site. For the annual projection (K2).
data_description.living_area_m2: For consumption per m² and the energy certificate class (K2).

cost.name: Cost
cost.description: Gross prices. The energy price is suggested from the energy dashboard if the heat pump meter is set up there.

data_description.tariff_price: Price per kWh of heat pump electricity (K1, K2).
data_description.tariff_base_fee: Only the additional standing charge per year for a separate heat pump meter; leave empty without one.
data_description.household_price: For comparison: is the separate heat pump tariff worth it (K3)?
data_description.reference_fuel_price: For comparison, e.g. gas: cost per kWh including the share of the standing charge (K1, K2).
data_description.reference_efficiency: Share of the billed fuel that arrives as heat. Gas condensing boilers reach 0.86 on average in field tests, based on the gross calorific value that gas is billed by.

evaluation.name: Evaluation

data_description.window_days: How many days back are evaluated.
data_description.data_since: Older data is ignored, e.g. before the interface was installed.

evaluation.description: The recorder only keeps its retention period (default 10 days); InfluxDB goes further back.

error.invalid_capacity_table: The minimum capacity does not have the expected format. Example: "35:" followed by indented "-7: 3.9", "2: 3.5", "7: 3.5".

flow_temperature.name: Audit 2 flow temperature as low as possible

flow_ratio.name: T3 flow ratio circuit to heat pump

heat_pump_spread.name: T4 heat pump spread and flow

dhw_draw.name: W6 hot water use and turnover

options.auto: Automatic: InfluxDB if set up, otherwise recorder

options.esphome_ecodan: Mitsubishi Ecodan with ESPHome (esphome-ecodan-hp, e.g. Mahtanar)

options.data_basis: Data basis – can the measurements be trusted? (recommended)
options.efficiency: Efficiency – how well does the heat pump work?
options.flow_temperature: Flow temperature – does it heat hotter than needed?
options.capacity: Capacity – does the heat pump fit the house?
options.dhw: Hot water – efficient, hygienic and at the right time?
options.cost: Cost – what does the heat cost, is the tariff worth it?

options.rotation: Alternating weeks (e.g. 1 week here, 1 week there)

user.title: Add audit
user.description: Which audit should run in addition? To disable an audit, delete its entry.{missing}

error.missing_roles: Required measurements are missing for this audit. Without them it stays “not assessable”. Map them via “Reconfigure” of the main entry.

user.title: Add event
user.description: A change to the system, e.g. heating curve adjusted or hydraulic balancing. The efficiency, flow temperature and capacity audits then only evaluate data after the latest event, so nothing is averaged across a change.

data_description.note: What exactly was changed, e.g. “parallel shift −1 K”.

reconfigure.title: Edit event
reconfigure.description: A change to the system, e.g. heating curve adjusted or hydraulic balancing. The efficiency, flow temperature and capacity audits then only evaluate data after the latest event, so nothing is averaged across a change.

data_description.note: What exactly was changed, e.g. “parallel shift −1 K”.

user.title: Household member
user.description: For the hot water demand (W5, W6). The audit compares the measured use with what is usual for this household.

data_description.name: Only to tell people apart, e.g. first name or “child 1”.
data_description.birth_year: For typical habits by age if showers and baths are left empty. Small children take baths rather than showers.
data_description.presence: When the person lives here, e.g. alternating weeks for children who also live with the other parent.
data_description.showers_per_week: Leave empty for a typical value by age.
data_description.baths_per_week: Leave empty for a typical value by age.
data_description.shower_time: For the charging time (W5): an afternoon window does not fit if people shower in the morning.

reconfigure.title: Change person
reconfigure.description: For the hot water demand (W5, W6).

data_description.name: Only to tell people apart, e.g. first name or “child 1”.
data_description.birth_year: For typical habits by age if showers and baths are left empty. Small children take baths rather than showers.
data_description.presence: When the person lives here, e.g. alternating weeks for children who also live with the other parent.
data_description.showers_per_week: Leave empty for a typical value by age.
data_description.baths_per_week: Leave empty for a typical value by age.
data_description.shower_time: For the charging time (W5): an afternoon window does not fit if people shower in the morning.

data_description.rotation_start: A day on which a period here begins (may be in the past); the pattern repeats from there. For “certain days” the anchor for “every n-th week”.
data_description.every_n_weeks: 1 = every week, 2 = every other week (e.g. every other weekend).
data_description.share_pct: If no fixed pattern fits: rough share, e.g. 30 %.

data_description.share_pct: If no fixed pattern fits: rough share, e.g. 30 %.
